title: Detached per-attempt Git worktree materializer
description: Objective: create the missing physical workspace allocator for one exact server-authorized Foundation attempt. MEASURED at HEAD f81ab75: @moe/runner has scope observers and manifest sealers but no worktree add/checkout/materialization production symbol; task-e17da1c explicitly excluded scratch-worktree I/O. Deliverable: a public @moe/runner Node adapter that derives a target only from catalog-owned sourceRepositoryRoot/worktreeParent plus server-owned project/attempt identity, creates a detached Git worktree at the exact 40/64-hex base, verifies containment/HEAD/clean state, supports exact replay adoption, and performs identity-fenced release/quarantine. NOT in scope: resolving repositoryRef/scopeRef, choosing declared paths, scanning result bytes, daemon persistence, provider launch, branch mutation, merge, staging, or push. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/workspace/worktree-materializer-contract.ts/.js, worktree-materializer-node.ts/.js, worktree-materializer-node.test.ts, packages/runner/src/index.ts, packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts. Consumer: the prepare-before-launch lifecycle task created by this split; record its exact id before completion. Verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck; $a=$LASTEXITCODE; pnpm --filter @moe/runner test; $b=$LASTEXITCODE; Write-Host "RUNNER_TC=$a RUNNER_TEST=$b"; if ($a -ne 0 -or $b -ne 0) { exit 1 }`, with nonzero printed test counts.
definitionOfDone: The @moe/runner bare root exports a frozen worktree materializer contract whose input has no caller-selected target path, branch, ref, checkout flags, shell command, environment, or cleanup path; target identity is deterministically derived from catalog-owned worktreeParent and server-owned project/attempt identities.

The Node adapter invokes Git through argv with shell:false and the repository's hermetic Git environment, creates a detached worktree at the exact admitted base, then verifies realpath containment under worktreeParent, exact HEAD, and clean porcelain state before returning a frozen assignment.

Replay adopts only an existing worktree whose derived path, source repository, base, realpath, HEAD, and clean state all match; collision, partial creation, wrong HEAD, non-detached/dirty state, repository escape, ambiguous ownership, or command/output overflow refuses with distinct stable code and layer and never guesses.

Release/removal requires the exact assignment identity and proven terminal caller intent; mismatch or cleanup uncertainty refuses and retains/quarantines the tree rather than deleting an unknown path. No API stages, commits, merges, pushes, resets, or touches the shared development checkout.

Focused tests include a real temporary Git repository and worktree with spaces, Windows path/argv behavior plus platform-neutral containment arms, replay/collision/crash residues, a nonzero hostile roster, and exact code/layer assertions; mutations enabling shell execution or adopting a wrong HEAD redden named tests.

The exact production consumer task id is recorded, runner typecheck/test both exit 0 with nonzero counts, all production files target <=250 lines and stay below 400, and plain Node loads each new LF bridge.
taskRails: Runtime worktrees may be created only inside test temp repositories during this task; do not create a sibling worktree of D:/projexts/moe-next or disturb the shared checkout.
Never accept a command/request path or Git ref as workspace authority; the upstream catalog and server attempt identity are the only inputs allowed to select location/base.
Use argv-based Git with shell:false and cross-platform hermetic environment handling; no shell string, broad staging, branch checkout, commit, merge, push, reset, or stash.
A cleanup uncertainty retains bytes and refuses; it never recursively deletes an unverified or escaped path.

implementationPlan.description: Replay adoption + identity-fenced release/quarantine, TDD RED first: adoption succeeds ONLY when derived path, source repository, base, realpath, HEAD, and clean state ALL match (vary exactly one per refusal test — co-variation hides holes); collision (path exists, wrong content), partial creation (worktree dir present but git metadata absent — simulate by mkdir), wrong HEAD, non-detached (branch checked out), dirty tree, repository escape (symlinked parent redirecting outside worktreeParent), ambiguous ownership each refuse with their exact code. Release: `git worktree remove` gated on the SAME identity fence (path+base+repo match) — releasing an unmatched tree refuses to QUARANTINE disposition instead of deleting (never destroy bytes the fence cannot prove ours; the shared-worktree hazard class in this very repo is the cautionary tale).
implementationPlan.note: Replay adoption + identity-fenced release/quarantine, all against a REAL temp git repo. Adoption: an exact replay returns adopted:true on the same realpath, and non-vacuity is proved ON DISK — readdirSync(parent) equals exactly [leaf] and `git worktree list --porcelain` counts 2 (main + one), so a double-create would redden. Refusal roster varies EXACTLY ONE fact per arm (co-variation would let one guard answer for two): wrong HEAD (checkout --detach HEAD~1) -> HEAD_MISMATCH; branch checked out -> NOT_DETACHED; dirty tree -> DIRTY; gutted .git -> PARTIAL; tree renamed outside the parent with a junction (symlink on POSIX) left behind so git still reports the registered path while its REALPATH escapes -> ESCAPED. Collision arm: a foreign directory sitting on the derived path refuses COLLISION and its bytes are still there afterwards. Release: RELEASED only on the proven path, and the SOURCE checkout is asserted untouched (HEAD identical, porcelain empty) plus idempotent on a second call. Retention roster (3 arms, each asserting the tree survives AND the registration count stays 2): ATTEMPT_ACTIVE -> RELEASE_NOT_TERMINAL; an assignment whose attemptId no longer derives its leaf -> RELEASE_FENCE_MISMATCH; an assignment naming a path outside its own parent -> RELEASE_FENCE_MISMATCH. A tree whose HEAD moved is QUARANTINED (ok:true, bytes retained) rather than deleted; a dirty tree makes `git worktree remove` refuse and that becomes RELEASE_UNCERTAIN — no --force anywhere, and the unsaved file is asserted still present. Deviation from plan wording: the adapter's release/adoption code landed in step 2 as one coherent module rather than RED-first here; step 6's mutation drills are what prove these tests actually bind. implementationPlan.note: Real-git suite rounded out; 26 passed / Test Files 1 passed. temporaryRepository() is a PRIVATE copy of the scope-git.test.ts pattern (no cross-suite helper import, no shared harness extracted), guarded by describe.skipIf(!gitAvailable()). 64-hex acceptance is proved END TO END, not by a unit arm: temporaryRepository("sha256") runs `git init --object-format=sha256` (probed available here: git 2.54.0.windows.1), the arm asserts the base matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ BEFORE materializing so a silent fallback to a sha1 repo cannot green it, and HEAD is read back at the 64-hex commit. Windows path realities: worktreeParent already contains a space in every real-git arm, and a dedicated case pushes the derived path past 200 chars. MEASURED git ceiling on this host: `worktree add --detach` succeeds at a 212-char target and refuses a 222-char one with `fatal: '$GIT_DIR' too big` — well BELOW the 260-char MAX_PATH that core.longpaths (unset here, `git config --get core.longpaths` exit 1) governs, so the widely-assumed 260 boundary is not the real one. The padding is therefore COMPUTED (205 - parent.length - leaf.length - 2) instead of hard-coded off one machine's temp dir, with expect(padding).toBeGreaterThan(0) as the non-vacuity guard; past the ceiling git's own failure arrives as the bounded COMMAND_FAILED already asserted by the absent-base arm, not a crash. Timeouts: describe raised 30s -> 60s and the two per-arm rosters pinned at 180s, because each builds one whole repository PER ARM (measured 39s for the five-arm roster on a loaded host) — same repair class as 64884d7/9f52c54.
